# jtoken

> Compress JSON-shaped documents for LLM prompts with fewer tokens — lossless, reproducible, stdlib-only.

jtoken encodes plain JSON, MongoDB shell/Extended JSON, and Elasticsearch hits into a short line-oriented format and can decode it back exactly (lossless round-trip). Measured savings (tiktoken, cl100k_base): −11.4% Elasticsearch hits, −19.1% MongoDB documents, −13.2% nested API events, −14.2% overall on the bundled benchmark.

## When to use

- RAG pipelines fit more retrieved JSON documents into the context window.
- Agent prompts include API/webhook payloads that repeat keys.
- You need to reconstruct the exact original data after compression (context sidecar).

## Install

```bash
pip install jtoken
# with tokenizer-accurate counting:
pip install "jtoken[tiktoken]"
```

## Quick reference

```python
import jtoken

# plain encode/decode (dict in, text out, dict back)
text = jtoken.encode({"user": "alice", "premium": True, "ref": None})
data = jtoken.decode(text)          # lossless for scalar/nested dicts
assert data == {"user": "alice", "premium": True, "ref": None}

# full-fidelity document workflow (dialects, lossless round-trip)
text, context = jtoken.encode_document(raw_json_text, source="auto")
restored = jtoken.decode_document(text, target="elastic_hit", context=context)

# measure token savings
stats = jtoken.token_savings(data, model="gpt-4o", backend="tiktoken")
print(stats)  # jtoken: X tokens | json: Y tokens | saved: Z (P%)

# CLI
# jtoken encode -f doc.json
# jtoken stats --model gpt-4o --backend tiktoken -f doc.json
```
